notes: Legacy logs mix hosts; only /neuwirth/ routes are included.
Legacy bytes are response bodies; JSON bytes include headers. Do not treat these as exact bandwidth comparisons.
IP allocations and user agents do not identify the operator.
Oct14 is partial and excluded from completed-day tables.

limits: IP registration, BGP origin and user agent are distinct evidence; none identifies a proxy customer.
The code200 feed was retrieved on October 14 and matched against October 13 requests. It lists externally announced ranges and may not cover all code200 infrastructure.
A /16 is an aggregation bin, not an assertion of common ownership. Registry lookups represent sampled suballocations unless covers_entire_grouped_prefix is true.
Network group rows below 20 requests are omitted; repository totals include them.
Legacy response sizes exclude headers; newer JSON sizes include them.
HTTP 200s count individual URLs and responses, including historical views, files, feeds and Git protocol URLs. They are not visits or unique files.
No inference is made that the post-Anubis crawl belongs to Meta.
The effect of difficulty 4 requires a subsequent observation window.
Synthetic difficulty-4 verification user agents are excluded from the repository aggregation.

meta_oct1_3.attribution: Declared Meta user agents and Meta-registered source addresses corroborate each other. This does not attribute the later Linux/Chrome crawl.

scope: HTTP requests whose path begins /neuwirth/; no unique-visitor estimate
